story.name: CATS: a summer-peak week in California
story.description: Generation, the transmission network by voltage, wildfire exposure and a week of dispatch, built by an agent through MCP.

steps.narration: **CATS, the California Test System**, is a synthetic grid on California's real geography: 8,870 buses and 3,892 generators, built from public data. Each circle is a power plant, sized by installed capacity and colored by technology: about 55 GW of thermal, hydro and other plants, plus 18 GW of wind and solar.

perspective.name: CATS 1. Generation capacity
perspective.description: Generators sized by installed MW, colored by technology.

steps.narration: **500 kV: 123 lines, about 7,500 km.** Line width shows the thermal rating. The 500 kV backbone runs the length of the state and carries the largest ratings in the system, up to 8.4 GW per line.

perspective.name: CATS 2. Lines, 500 kV
perspective.description: 500 kV lines; width shows the thermal rating.

steps.narration: **230 kV: 1,258 lines, about 13,300 km.** The 230 kV network ties the backbone to the large load centers around the Bay Area, the Central Valley and Southern California.

perspective.name: CATS 3. Lines, 230 kV
perspective.description: 230 kV lines; width shows the thermal rating.

steps.narration: **115 kV: 2,209 lines, about 13,000 km.** 115 kV lines distribute power within each region.

perspective.name: CATS 4. Lines, 115 kV
perspective.description: 115 kV lines; width shows the thermal rating.

steps.narration: **66 kV: 6,565 lines, about 20,300 km.** The sub-transmission network is the densest layer: more than half of all lines, with the smallest ratings.

perspective.name: CATS 5. Lines, 66 kV
perspective.description: 66 kV lines; width shows the thermal rating.

steps.narration: **Data from another source, added by an agent.** The agent loaded the CPUC High Fire-Threat District map (red: Tier 3 Extreme, orange: Tier 2 Elevated) and CAL FIRE's 2019 fire perimeters (white), and laid them over the grid. About 10% of CATS line length is in Tier 3 and 22% in Tier 2, including 1,036 km of 500 kV lines (14%).

perspective.name: CATS 6. Wildfire exposure
perspective.description: CPUC fire-threat tiers and CAL FIRE 2019 perimeters over the network.

steps.narration: **12–18 August 2019, hour by hour**, from a PowerSimulations (Sienna) economic dispatch. Circles show generation inside available capacity; lines show loading from green to red. The chart tray follows the clock: watch solar ramp up and down each day while demand peaks in the late afternoon.

perspective.name: CATS 7. A week of summer peak
perspective.description: Hourly dispatch and line loading, 12-18 Aug 2019, with generation and demand charts.

chartSpec.name: CATS_Summer_peak_2019__system_generation_stacked
chartSpec.sql_template: WITH gen_by_dg AS (  SELECT cm.category AS display_group,          SUM(COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (entity_id, category)))   FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__generation g   JOIN ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__catmap__display_group cm     ON g.entity_id = cm.entity_id   GROUP BY cm.category), gen_long AS (  SELECT * FROM gen_by_dg   UNPIVOT (mw FOR timestamp IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE display_group)))), vre_entities AS (  SELECT entity_id FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__catmap__display_group   WHERE category IN ('Land-based Wind', 'Offshore Wind', 'Onshore Wind', 'PV', 'UPV', 'VRE', 'Wind', 'dPV')), gen_unpivot AS (  SELECT entity_id, ts, val FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__generation   UNPIVOT (val FOR ts IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE entity_id)))   WHERE entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM vre_entities)), avail_unpivot AS (  SELECT entity_id, ts, val FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__availability   UNPIVOT (val FOR ts IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE entity_id)))   WHERE entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM vre_entities)), curt_long AS (  SELECT 'Curtailment' AS display_group,          g.ts AS timestamp,          SUM(GREATEST(0, a.val - g.val))::DOUBLE AS mw   FROM gen_unpivot g   JOIN avail_unpivot a     ON g.entity_id = a.entity_id AND g.ts = a.ts   GROUP BY g.ts) SELECT display_group, timestamp, mw FROM gen_long UNION ALL SELECT display_group, timestamp, mw FROM curt_long ORDER BY timestamp, display_group

chartSpec.name: CATS_Summer_peak_2019__system_demand
chartSpec.sql_template: WITH load_long AS (  SELECT entity_id, ts, val FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__load   UNPIVOT (val FOR ts IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE entity_id)))), gen_long AS (  SELECT entity_id, ts, val FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__generation   UNPIVOT (val FOR ts IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE entity_id)))), total_demand AS (  SELECT ts, -SUM(val) AS demand_mw   FROM load_long GROUP BY ts), vre_gen AS (  SELECT g.ts, SUM(g.val) AS vre_mw   FROM gen_long g   JOIN ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__catmap__display_group cm     ON g.entity_id = cm.entity_id   WHERE cm.category IN ('Land-based Wind', 'Offshore Wind', 'Onshore Wind', 'PV', 'UPV', 'VRE', 'Wind', 'dPV')   GROUP BY g.ts) SELECT ts AS timestamp, 'Native Load' AS series, demand_mw::DOUBLE AS mw FROM total_demand UNION ALL SELECT d.ts AS timestamp, 'Net Load' AS series,        (d.demand_mw - COALESCE(v.vre_mw, 0))::DOUBLE AS mw FROM total_demand d LEFT JOIN vre_gen v ON d.ts = v.ts ORDER BY timestamp, series

steps.narration: **Thursday 15 August, 16:00: the week's peak, 39.7 GW.** The Los Angeles basin holds most of the heavily loaded lines: across the system, 69 branches are at 90% of their rating or more. The average loading chart shows the same daily rhythm all week.

perspective.name: CATS 8. The peak hour
perspective.description: Thursday 15 Aug 2019 16:00, 39.7 GW; the Los Angeles basin, where most heavily loaded lines are.

chartSpec.name: CATS_Summer_peak_2019__loading_avg
chartSpec.sql_template: WITH flow_long AS (  SELECT entity_id, ts, val FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__line_flow   UNPIVOT (val FOR ts IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE entity_id)))) SELECT f.ts AS timestamp,        (AVG(ABS(f.val) / r.rating_mw) * 100)::DOUBLE AS pct FROM flow_long f JOIN ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__branch_ratings r ON f.entity_id = r.name WHERE r.rating_mw > 0 GROUP BY f.ts ORDER BY f.ts

chartSpec.name: CATS_Summer_peak_2019__system_generation_stacked
chartSpec.sql_template: WITH gen_by_dg AS (  SELECT cm.category AS display_group,          SUM(COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE (entity_id, category)))   FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__generation g   JOIN ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__catmap__display_group cm     ON g.entity_id = cm.entity_id   GROUP BY cm.category), gen_long AS (  SELECT * FROM gen_by_dg   UNPIVOT (mw FOR timestamp IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE display_group)))), vre_entities AS (  SELECT entity_id FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__catmap__display_group   WHERE category IN ('Land-based Wind', 'Offshore Wind', 'Onshore Wind', 'PV', 'UPV', 'VRE', 'Wind', 'dPV')), gen_unpivot AS (  SELECT entity_id, ts, val FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__generation   UNPIVOT (val FOR ts IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE entity_id)))   WHERE entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM vre_entities)), avail_unpivot AS (  SELECT entity_id, ts, val FROM ext_gat.CATS_Summer_peak_2019__availability   UNPIVOT (val FOR ts IN (COLUMNS(* EXCLUDE entity_id)))   WHERE entity_id IN (SELECT entity_id FROM vre_entities)), curt_long AS (  SELECT 'Curtailment' AS display_group,          g.ts AS timestamp,          SUM(GREATEST(0, a.val - g.val))::DOUBLE AS mw   FROM gen_unpivot g   JOIN avail_unpivot a     ON g.entity_id = a.entity_id AND g.ts = a.ts   GROUP BY g.ts) SELECT display_group, timestamp, mw FROM gen_long UNION ALL SELECT display_group, timestamp, mw FROM curt_long ORDER BY timestamp, display_group
